title: Microcontext eviction hypotheses log
content:
Purpose and scope:

This is a personal scratchpad collecting hypotheses, quick sketches, and an API-config shape for a light-weight 'microcontext' eviction mechanism. The goal is to design something that sits between big KV cache eviction and client-side TTLs: cheap, low-latency heuristics to evict small conversational context slices and to surface prefetch hints for warmups.

Motivation / problem statement:
- Some customers have very spiky per-session token patterns: long tails of rarely-reused context cause memory pressure on serving nodes.
- Full-blown LRU on token-level state is too costly to maintain across tenants when using dense KV caches.
- We want a cheap, tunable layer that: (a) removes low-value microcontext to free memory, (b) emits signals for client-side prefetch heuristics or rehydration, and (c) is observable/undoable for debugging.

Constraints and desiderata:
- Extremely low CPU overhead per decision (< 200ns ideally), amortized across batching.
- Deterministic under same inputs (for easier replay) but parameterizable per-tenant.
- Expose a compact config DSL so product folks can test tradeoffs without runtime code changes.
- Telemetry should be able to attach eviction cause and a short trace id to rehydrate if needed.

Design primitives (v0 sketches):
1) Microcontext unit: "slice"
   - Small unit (1-8 utterances or N tokens up to 1024).
   - Identified by (session_id, slice_seq) and a short checksum.

2) Scoring signals (cheap approximations):
   - last_access_delta_ms (time since slice last used) bucketed (0-1s, 1-10s, 10-60s, 60s-10m, >10m)
   - reuse_count (small integer saturating at 7)
   - size_tokens (bucketed tiny/medium/large)
   - affinitized_route (boolean: indicates if this slice is pinned to a hot route)
   - negative_feedback_flag (boolean: if client marked slice useless)

3) Policy API (config DSL)
   - policy kind: {conservative|balanced|aggressive|pinned-only}
   - soft_ttl_ms: string (e.g., "30s"), after which slices become evictable candidates
   - reuse_threshold: int (min reuse_count to keep)
   - eviction_budget_per_min: int (max slices to evict per min per node)
   - fallback_action: {drop|snapshot-to-cold|mark-archival}
   - prefetch_hint_threshold: float (score above which we emit a prefetch hint)

Example policy (yaml-like textual):

policy: balanced
soft_ttl_ms: "45s"
reuse_threshold: 2
eviction_budget_per_min: 500
fallback_action: "snapshot-to-cold"
prefetch_hint_threshold: 0.6

4) Scoring function (cheap):
   score = w_time * bucket(last_access_delta_ms) + w_reuse * min(reuse_count,7)/7 + w_size * inv_bucket(size_tokens)
   - weights are small integers in [0..4] and normalized server-side.
   - bucket() returns 0..1 from precomputed LUT to avoid branches.

API shape for eviction decisions (compact json-lines over internal wire):
- EvictCandidate {
    "session": "s-xxxxx",
    "slice_seq": "42",
    "checksum": "f3a1",
    "score": "0.72",
    "cause": "ttl+low_reuse",
    "policy_id": "balanced-2025-02",
    "last_access_ms": "120000",
    "size_tokens": "128",
    "trace_id": "t-3309"
  }

- PrefetchHint {
    "session": "s-xxxxx",
    "slice_seq": "43",
    "predicted_cost": "0.02",
    "prob_reuse": "0.65",
    "hint_ttl": "20s",
    "hint_origin": "micro-evict-v0"
  }

Eviction lifecycle (quick notes):
- candidate selection -> mark (soft) -> asynchronously decide actual eviction respecting node budget -> fallback action executed (could snapshot to coldstore, emit telemetry + hint)
- Marked slices stay addressable (reads cause rehydration) for back-compat; actual memory free only after physical drop or successful snapshot.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Snapshot cost vs drop: for large slices snapshotting to cold (s3/cold-kv) costs network + IOPS but reduces tail rehydration latency. When to choose?
- Budgeting correctness: cross-node eviction budgets need careful accounting for tenanted pools. Should budgets be per-tenant-per-node or global-per-node?
- Is reuse_count biased by pathological loops (clients replaying session)? Add decay factor?
- Determinism vs adaptivity: I favor deterministic scoring for replayability and easier debugging; but adaptivity (online weight tuning) could improve economics. Maybe deterministic + periodic recalibration.

Telemetry schema (minimal fields for traceability):
- evt: "evict_mark" | "evict_commit" | "prefetch_emit" | "rehydrate_request"
- session, slice_seq, policy_id, node_id, score, reason, trace_id, timestamp_ms
- sample logs should include the last 2 access deltas and reuse_count to debug evictions

Debugging / observability UX notes:
- Console view: show for a session the currently-marked slices with small inline "why" (score breakdown), ability to force-restore a slice (good for customer support)
- Allow manual override per-session in console (UI toggle) that sets policy to pinned-only for a session id

Quick simulation plan (how to test):
1) Offline sim harness using production traces (ENG-8241) to compute memory saved vs false-evictions (cases where evicted slice was needed within Xs)
2) Small canary (1% traffic) with conservative policy; emit telemetry and compute rehydrate latency delta and extra cold-store IO
3) Run A/B for balanced vs conservative policies and report cost-per-1000-requests and tail-latency regressions

Implementation notes / perf ideas:
- Keep scoring LUTs in L1-friendly arrays, avoid hashmap access on hot path.
- Store small bitfield (8 bits) per slice to encode bucketed signals (time_bucket:3 reuse_count:3 flags:2) to compress decisions into 1 atomic read.
- Do not serialize full slice to the eviction pipeline; only send compact candidate record and checksum.

UX edge-cases observed in sketches:
- Multi-client sessions where one client churns slices aggressively, another wants full history. Need per-client affinity tag on slice to avoid punishing remote clients.
- Tenant bulk-evictions during maintenance -> service impact. Provide a maintenance policy mode that switches fallback_action to "mark-no-commit" and requires manual commit.

Notes to self / TODOs:
- Add sample offline script for scoring and include pseudo-code.
- Spin up small prototyping PR to wire the marking pipeline in runtime (refer to PR template in linked_artifacts).
- Check with SRE about node_id accounting: is there an existing per-node budget meter we can reuse? (ping @Devon)

Rough pseudo-code (very rough):

// compute bitfield from slice metadata (hot path)
bitfield = pack(time_bucket, min(reuse_count,7), flags)
score = lut_time[time_bucket]*w_time + lut_reuse[min(reuse_count,7)]*w_reuse + lut_size[size_bucket]*w_size
if score < policy.threshold: continue
if budget_available(node): mark_candidate(...)

End.

Small log excerpt (example):
2025-02-21T11:02:32.442Z evict_mark session=s-1712 slice=7 score=0.21 cause=ttl node=n-17 policy=balanced-2025-02 trace=t-3309
2025-02-21T11:02:32.470Z evict_commit session=s-1712 slice=7 node=n-17 action=snapshot-to-cold snap_id=snap-224

If you read this and have ideas: add short note inline (collaborators) or drop a quick link to a sim result. I'm trying to keep this notebook intentionally messy so it's easy to copy fragments into a PR or a Confluence page later.
